```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
res <- readRDS(file.path(params$dir, "results.rds"))
img <- function(name) {
    knitr::include_graphics(file.path(params$dir, paste0(name, ".png")))
}
tab <- function(x, ...) {
    knitr::kable(x, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), row.names = FALSE, ...)
}
perf <- res$perf
secs <- function(step) perf$seconds[perf$step == step]
bins <- res$bins
mmd <- res$permanova[res$permanova$distance == "MMD", ]
bc <- res$permanova[res$permanova$distance == "Bray-Curtis", ]
gated <- bins[bins$setting == "similarity + coverage", ]
ungated <- bins[bins$setting == "similarity only", ]
ungated_edges <- res$pairs$pairs[abs(res$pairs$min_sim - 0.7) < 1e-9]
removed <- 1 - gated$edges / ungated_edges
big <- function(v) format(v, big.mark = ",")
in_pick <- function(i) res$members$bin == res$picks$bin[i]
n_m <- function(i) sum(in_pick(i))
n_ko <- function(i) sum(in_pick(i) & !is.na(res$members$KO))
```

# Summary

* **Scale.** `r format(res$data[["proteins"]], big.mark = ",")` proteins and
  `r res$data[["samples"]]` samples ran end to end in
  `r round(sum(perf$seconds) / 60, 1)` minutes of timed steps on
  `r res$workers` workers.
* **Beta diversity.** Diet explains R² = `r mmd$R2` under MMD against
  `r bc$R2` under Bray-Curtis (PERMANOVA, permutations within mouse).
* **Coverage gate.** At the default floor (predicted TM-score 0.7),
  requiring an alignment over half of both sequences removes
  `r round(100 * removed)`% of the edges and shrinks the largest connected
  component from `r if (nrow(ungated)) big(ungated$largest_component) else "?"`
  to `r big(gated$largest_component)` proteins, giving
  `r big(gated$bins)` bins.
* **MCL.** `bin_proteins()` took `r secs("bin_proteins, coverage gate")` s
  at inflation 2 on the gated graph, whose largest component holds
  `r big(gated$largest_component)` proteins as one dense matrix.
* **Function.** KOfamScan gives `r round(100 * res$kofam[["with a KO"]] /
  res$kofam[["proteins"]])`% of proteins a KO; the t-SNE map is coloured by
  their KEGG BRITE category.
* **Differential abundance.** `r res$deseq[["diet_significant"]]` of
  `r format(res$deseq[["bins_tested"]], big.mark = ",")` bins respond to diet
  (DESeq2 LRT, BH 0.05).
* **Checks.** Both file readers return the same proteins, sequences and
  embeddings at full size.

# Data

Rarefied once (seed 1), baseline samples dropped, proteins over 3,000 aa
removed, as on the project site.

```{r data}
tab(data.frame(quantity = names(res$data),
    value = vapply(res$data, format, "", big.mark = ",")))
```

Annotations come from Extended Data Table 6, joined on *Protein Identifier*
with a fallback to the species-code column, keeping a match only where the
residue count agrees.

```{r annotation}
tab(data.frame(join = names(res$annotation), proteins = unname(res$annotation)))
```

# Reading embeddings from files

The cached TM-Vec embeddings were written out in the `tmvec build-db` layout
(`.npz`) and the `tmvec embed` HDF5 layout, then read back with
`read_embeddings()`.

```{r readers}
r <- cbind(file = rownames(res$readers), res$readers,
    MB = res$file_MB,
    seconds = c(secs("read_embeddings, tmvec .npz"),
        secs("read_embeddings, HDF5")))
r$max_abs_embedding_diff <- format(r$max_abs_embedding_diff, digits = 2)
tab(r)
```

# Embedding map by function

KOfamScan (prokaryote profiles) assigned a KO to
`r big(res$kofam[["with a KO"]])` of `r big(res$kofam[["proteins"]])`
proteins. Each KO is coloured by its KEGG BRITE level-B category; the
`r big(res$kofam[["KO in more than one category"]])` proteins whose KO sits in
several categories take the one holding most of its pathways, then the one
KEGG lists first. Same t-SNE coordinates as above.

```{r kofam}
tab(data.frame(quantity = names(res$kofam), proteins = unname(res$kofam)))
```

# The most responsive annotated bins

The three most responsive bins with more than one member and at least two
annotated members.

```{r picks}
tab(res$picks)
tab(res$members)
```

`r res$picks$bin[1]` is `r n_m(1)` GH92 family glycosyl hydrolases (the
family of exo-α-mannosidases), higher on the yeast diet, whose cell walls are
rich in mannan. The other two are the caution: `r res$picks$bin[2]` holds an
S-adenosylmethionine synthase, a GH109 protein and four unannotated proteins,
and `r res$picks$bin[3]` a trimeric autotransporter adhesin, a
pyrrolidone-carboxylate peptidase and an ABC multidrug efflux protein. Each
shares a structural bin, not a function.

KOfamScan's per-family thresholds are stricter than the study's annotation:
it assigns a KO to `r n_ko(1)` of the `r n_m(1)` GH92 proteins, so the bin
carries a function to members a profile search leaves unlabelled.

```{r bin, out.width = "70%"}
if (file.exists(file.path(params$dir, "bin.png"))) img("bin")
```

The same t-SNE coordinates, with these bins' members coloured:

```{r tsne, out.width = "75%"}
if (file.exists(file.path(params$dir, "tsne.png"))) img("tsne")
```

# Run time and memory

Wall-clock seconds and peak R heap per step (max-used cells × 8 bytes, so
everything live at the time counts), on `r res$workers` `BiocParallel`
workers; forked alignment workers are not counted.

```{r perf}
tab(perf)
```

* The dense protein-by-protein matrices set the memory ceiling: about
  `r max(perf$peak_R_GB)` GB at `r big(res$data[["proteins"]])` proteins,
  growing with the square of the protein count.
* `sample_mmd()` spends most of its time in `stats::dist()` over all
  protein pairs, which is single-threaded.
* MCL cost follows the largest connected component, because the `MCL`
  package holds each component as a dense matrix and stops only when two
  iterations are identical.
* The HDF5 reader is slower than the `.npz` reader because `rhdf5` reads one
  group per protein.
